Subject: Retention & redaction options for PHI in Private deployment

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Lumen Health is evaluating Redwood Private for a pilot that will process claims and clinical notes. Our security and compliance teams have two quick asks we need clarified before we move to procurement:

1) Retention limits: we have a regulatory requirement to retain claims records for 7 years, but patient encounter notes for adults can be 3 years; minors require different retention and additional deletion triggers. Can you summarize how Redwood supports per-tenant retention policies and whether we can set per-data-type retention windows?

2) Redaction/deletion semantics: in some workflows we need the ability to (a) remove specific PII/PHI fields from model inputs and from any persisted caches/traces, (b) permanently delete all data for a tenant upon contract termination, and (c) provide an auditable proof-of-deletion for e-discovery. Is there an API or playbook for these actions and what are the timelines/SLOs?

Also, our security team will want to see how you handle KV cache and any transient storage used by the inference runtime.

We're attaching a short list of the retention scenarios. Can you send a concise technical summary and propose a next-step: a short call with your product/security engineers or a checklist we can hand to our compliance team?

Thanks,
Claire Simmons

Subject: Re: Retention & redaction options for PHI in Private deployment

Hi Claire — really appreciate the clear list. Attaching a short technical summary and a matrix mapping data types to retention mechanisms. In brief:

- Per-tenant/field retention: Redwood Private supports tenant-scoped retention policies that can be scoped to data classes (claims, notes, transcripts). Policies are enforced at ingest and in background maintenance jobs.

- Multiple retention tiers: You can configure separate windows (e.g., 7y for claims, 3y for adult notes, conditional retention for minors) with policy inheritance and explicit overrides.

- Redaction vs deletion: We distinguish three operations:
  1) Field-level redaction (masking/pseudonymization) — replaces fields before persistence or before being retained in caches. Good for analytics/QA while preserving linkage if needed.
  2) Logical deletion (soft-delete) — marks records as deleted and removes them from normal serving paths; retained for a configurable legal-hold period.
  3) Physical purge (hard-delete) — irreversibly removes data from primary stores and triggers KV-cache eviction, background compaction, and ledger update for audit. Hard-delete is what you want for termination.

- KV cache & runtime artifacts: transient KV cache entries are configurable TTLs and are included in purge runs; our deletion pipeline explicitly scrubs KV cache and intermediate artifacts (tokens, prefetch buffers) for Private deployments.

- Proof of deletion/audit: deletion runs emit an auditable event with a signed checksum and retention-policy id which can be exported to your SIEM or included in a deletion report. We also can provide a time-stamped statement and the retention window that was applied.

I attached the 2-page summary and an XLS comparing redaction approaches. Proposed next step: a 30-min technical sync with our Security Engineering (Naomi) and Product (Marissa) to walk through the deletion API endpoints and what we can provide as evidence. Are you available tomorrow 10:00-10:30 ET?

Attachments: PHI-Retention-Options.pdf, redaction-approaches-compare.xlsx

Best,
Avery Johnson

Avery / Claire,

A couple of clarifying items from Security:

- Legal hold: We will require the ability to place a legal hold that supersedes scheduled deletion for specific subject IDs and case IDs. During hold, data must be immune to purge and flagged in audit exports. Can Redwood apply fine-grained holds (case-level) rather than tenant-level only?

- Minor-specific flows: For patients under 18, we need automatic revocation triggers (e.g., when DOB indicates minor at time-of-event) plus a workflow for guardian consent revocations that can accelerate deletion. Is there an event-driven hook to trigger immediate purge?

- Proof: The “signed checksum + event” looks good; can you include the list of storage locations that are covered by your deletion pipeline (S3 buckets, local SSDs on GPUs, cache layers, audit logs)? We need a mapping to satisfy our auditors.

If a short sync is easier, I can join tomorrow 10 ET. I loop Naomi from Redwood in case she wants to circle back to internal infra details.

— Jared
InfoSec, Lumen Health

Thanks all — recap and proposed owners:

Action items:
- Product (Marissa): produce a 1-page tech note listing the storage locations and exactly which are swept by the hard-delete pipeline (include S3 paths, object lifecycles, and local GPU SSD erase windows). Target: EOD 3/16.
- Security Engineering (Naomi): confirm ability to support case-level legal hold and document the mechanism (flagging + hold exemption) and the expected behavior during backup restores. Target: 3/17 COB.
- Runtime (Rishi): document KV-cache eviction timeline and the API for triggering an immediate eviction for a tenant or object id. Include any limits or backpressure impacts. Target: 3/17 COB.
- Sales (Avery): schedule the 30-min sync with Lumen Security/Procurement; provide the deletion playbook and the signed-cheksum sample.

Suggested sync time: tomorrow 10:00-10:30 ET — Claire/Jared let us know if that works and we will send a calendar invite with a short agenda.

Notes: we should avoid recommending field-level pseudonymization as the only control for regulated deletion — it can complicate proof-of-deletion workflows. Where possible recommend purge + tokenization for analytics copies that require re-identification under strict controls.

Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference
